Write TRUE if the statement is correct and FALSE if the statement is not correct. (i) God asked Adam questions to make him reflect on his disobedience. (ii) Noah was saved because he was perfect without sin. (iii) Abraham obeyed God even when he did not know the destination. (iv) The Law was given before the Exodus from Egypt. (v) Complaints in the wilderness showed lack of trust in God. (vi) Moses acted as both leader and mediator. (vii) Samson’s strength depended on his obedience to God. (viii) Saul accepted correction immediately. (ix) David’s repentance restored his relationship with God. (x) Prophets always delivered comforting messages. (xi) Covenant obedience was linked with blessing. (xii) Judges ruled Israel during peaceful times. Give short answers to the following questions: (i) Jacob had more than one wife. List three sons born to him. (ii) Mention any three types of offerings according to the Law. (iii) While at Rephidim, Moses struck the rock. (a) Why did the people complain? (b) What resulted from striking the rock? (iv) Give two reasons why Joseph was hated by his brothers. (v) Briefly describe how Jericho was captured. (vi) Deuteronomy 34 explains the death of Moses. (a) Where did he die? (b) Why did he die there? (c) How old was he? (d) Who buried him? (vii) Mention two roles played by judges in Israel. (viii) According to Genesis 9:20–27, state the outcome of Noah’s misuse of wine. (ix) What command did God give Israel as the key to life in Canaan? (Deut. 6:4–5) (x) Give two reasons why obedience was important in Israel’s covenant. Give short answers to the following questions: (i) “But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.” Joshua 24:15 (a) Who spoke these words? (b) To whom were the words spoken? (c) What historical situation led to this declaration? (d) What decision was Joshua urging the people to make? (e) State two lessons believers learn from this declaration. (ii) “Put off your shoes from your feet, because the place on which you stand is holy.” (a) Who was commanded to do this? (b) Where did this event take place? (c) Why was the place described as holy? (d) What does this command teach about approaching God? (iii) The fall of man is recorded in Genesis 3. (a) What command did God give to Adam and Eve? (b) How was this command broken? (c) Explain God’s punishment to the woman. (d) Explain God’s punishment to the man. (e) What does this passage teach about obedience and responsibility? (iv) “The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.” Exodus 14:14 (a) Who spoke these words? (b) In what situation were the words spoken? (c) What problem were the Israelites facing at that time? (d) How were these words fulfilled? (e) State one lesson learned from this event. (v) Isaac was ready to be sacrificed by his father. Genesis 22. (a) What instruction did God give Abraham concerning Isaac? (b) How did Isaac respond during the journey? (viii) While the Israelites were on their journey to Canaan, they crossed major water bodies. (a) Name two water bodies they crossed. (b) Under whose leadership was each crossing done? (c) How did God help the Israelites to cross safely? (d) What was the significance of these crossings to Israel’s faith?
